text:
[LTIM.2.5.1] A rule gated on a time-dependent condition **must fire once per
false → true edge** of the condition for a given matched fact wrapper, on the
pump at which the edge occurs, and **must not re-fire** on subsequent pumps
while the condition remains true. This edge-once behaviour is a consequence of
refraction ([LDET.5.3]) with [LDET.5.8]: a clock tick is not a change to the
LHS, so a fired activation stays refracted across pumps for as long as its
match persists.

A pump that ends at a firing limit leaves the activation unfired; it fires on a
later pump if its match persists until then.

**A condition that closes ends the match, and a reopening is a new edge.** When
the condition goes true → false, the match ends and its activation with it, as a
`within` window's does ([LTIM.2.7.2]); no memory of the firing outlives the
activation. When the condition goes false → true again for the same wrapper, the
new match fires. A gate that stays true once true fires once per wrapper; a
window that shuts and reopens, or a `now()` gate the wall clock crosses back and
forth ([LTIM.2.8.3]), fires once per opening.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_1__within_falls
idris.note: A `within` window on a fixed stamp changes at most once, true to false: it shuts and does not reopen for that entry, so 'a window that shuts and reopens' is a window on a new entry, a new wrapper.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_6__dwell_gate_rises
idris.note: WHICH GATES CAN REOPEN: a `dwell >= d` gate on a fixed stamp changes at most once, false to true, so it 'stays true once true' and the clause's once per edge is once per wrapper for it. Only a gate that reads the wall clock can reopen, which is [LTIM.2.8.3]'s last sentence.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__at_most_once_is_an_instance
idris.note: A rising gate's one edge, on the timer.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__edges_after_due
idris.note: A rising gate makes no edge once true.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__edges_are_first_due
idris.note: The one edge of the timer's gate, located.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__fires_on_the_first_due_tick
idris.note: Once per edge, and the timer's gate has its edge at the first due tick.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__timer_counts_are_edges
idris.note: Once per false-to-true edge, for the timer's gate.

idris.name: ltac_5_3__due_rising
idris.note: A rising gate: true once true.

idris.name: ldet_5_8__late_fires_once_clocked
idris.note: A gate that stays true once true fires once per wrapper: `rule late` fires in the third of four pumps and never again, `[0, 0, 1, 0]`, on the composed engine.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_2__unfired_are_born_clocked
idris.note: What the pump after a tick fires is exactly the matches the tick made: one firing per edge, on this engine's timed chain.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__closing_ends_clocked
idris.note: 'A condition that closes ends the match': under the view, the re-timed chain holds no activation whose match the new test refuses, fired or not.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__edge_once_clocked
idris.note: EDGE-ONCE ACROSS TWO SUCCESSIVE TICKS of this engine, for any gate: no match is made by both the tick to `c1` and the tick to `c2`, because the chain re-timed at `c1` carries the test at `c1` and the next tick re-times from it -- a match the second tick makes was refused at `c1`, which the first tick admitted. No hypothesis on the gate: Tick's `ltim_2_5_1__edge_once` needs `Ltim_2_5_1__rising` to carry a verdict from one tick's end to the next's start, and here the two are one clock. The clause's claim over a history -- a rising gate fires once per wrapper, the pump counts are the gate's rising edges -- is `ltim_2_5_1__rising_fires_at_most_once` (Rete/NetworkTwoClocks.idr) and `ltim_2_5_1__counts_are_edges` (Rete/NetworkEdges.idr).

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__expired_fact_cannot_reopen
idris.note: A wrapper that expired while the gate was shut is not there to reopen on: `[1, 0, 0, 0]`, computed. Once per edge is once per wrapper, and the wrapper is gone.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__reopening_is_unfired_clocked
idris.note: 'A reopening is a new edge': an activation whose match the tick made is unfired, whatever fired before the gate shut.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__second_edge_refires_clocked
idris.note: 'A window that shuts and reopens fires once per opening': `[1, 0, 1, 0]` over ticks 1 to 4 on the composed engine, computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_2367
idris.note: The window `{2, 3, 6, 7}`, the shape formal/tla/refraction_readings.tla and the conformance fixture `LTIM.2.5.1_window_reopens.json` share. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_2367_clocked
idris.note: ONE WINDOW, THREE MODELS: over ticks 1 to 7 the rule fires in the second pump and the sixth, `[0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0]`, one firing per opening -- the same answer formal/tla/refraction_readings.tla (`tick_edge_twice`, `1@2 1@6`), formal/tla/edge_once_firing.tla's `probe.refires` and the conformance fixture `LTIM.2.5.1_window_reopens.json` give.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_2367_gate
idris.note: That window as a time-dependent join test. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_2367_start
idris.note: The rule under that window loaded with one `Ping`. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_program
idris.note: The window rule's program. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_start
idris.note: The window rule loaded with one `Ping`. A fixture.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__action_free
idris.note: ACTION-FREE: every rule's action list is empty -- rules that only log, as [LDET.5.8]'s example does. The frame of B0 and B1.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__edges
idris.note: THE RISING EDGES of a gate over a history of ticks from a starting clock, one per tick: the clause's 'false to true edge', counted.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__action_free_mark
idris.note: Marking keeps a program action-free.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__action_free_tick
idris.note: So the tick keeps a program action-free.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__born_edge
idris.note: What a tick makes of one fact and the nil token: one match if the gate was false and is true, none otherwise. All four cases.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__counts_are_edges
idris.note: B2. THE COUNTS ARE THE EDGES: for one fact and one rule under ANY gate on the clock, with no actions and no deadline, the firings of ANY sequence of ticks from ANY starting clock are the gate's rising edges over that history, one count per pump. Once per false-to-true edge, for every gate and every history: a gate that stays true once true fires once, a window that shuts and reopens fires once per opening. Part A's `[1, 0, 1, 0]` is its instance.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__edge_at
idris.note: ONE TICK'S EDGE: 1 where the gate is false at the clock before the tick and true at the clock after it, else 0.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__edge_lt
idris.note: An edge count is below any fuel of two or more.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__gate
idris.note: A gate on the clock alone, as a timed test: `now() > t`, a window, any predicate of the clock. A fixture family.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__held_at
idris.note: The one rule's activations when quiescent: the `Ping` match, fired, if the gate is true; nothing if it is false. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_rule
idris.note: ONE FACT, ONE RULE, ANY GATE: the clocked network holding one `Ping`, one alpha admitting it, one chain whose single positive node carries the gate at the clock, no actions, no dependency row, no deadline; quiescent at the clock. A fixture family.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_rule_after
idris.note: What the tick and the run leave of the one rule's activations, from quiescence at the old gate value: quiescence at the new one. A gate that stays true keeps the fired match; one that closes ends it; one that opens makes a new match, which the run fires. All four cases.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_rule_born
idris.note: The matches the tick makes of the one rule are its edge.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_rule_pump
idris.note: ONE PUMP OF THE ONE RULE: from the quiescent state at a clock, the pump at a tick fires the edge and leaves the quiescent state at the new clock. B1 at the one rule.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_rule_quiescent
idris.note: The one rule is quiescent at either value of the gate.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_rule_tick
idris.note: The one rule after the tick and the run: the one rule at the new clock.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__pump_fires_the_born
idris.note: B1. THE PUMP FIRES THE BORN, on the composed engine: from a quiescent action-free state with an empty dependency table and nothing expiring at the new clock, the pump at a tick fires exactly as many times as the tick made matches over every timed chain, halts `Quiescent`, and leaves the state the tick made with every activation marked. Each born activation fires once and none twice. Inhabited by `ltim_2_5_1__one_rule_pump`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__run_marks_all
idris.note: B0. THE RUN IS ONE MARK PER UNFIRED ACTIVATION: under an action-free program, with fuel above the number of unfired activations, the run halts `Quiescent`, fires exactly that many times, and leaves every activation of every chain marked -- working memory, the alphas, the nodes, the tuples, the dependency table, the deadlines and the clock as they were. The frame is syntactic: a step under it is the marking of one activation and nothing else; a program with actions is outside it (Rete/NetworkFrame.idr has the general frame).

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__second_edge_refires_is_an_instance
idris.note: PART A'S `[1, 0, 1, 0]` IS AN INSTANCE OF B2: Rete/NetworkClocked.idr's executed witness is the edge theorem at the window gate, from clock 0, over the ticks 1, 2, 3, 4.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_edges
idris.note: The window's rising edges over ticks to 1, 2, 3, 4 are `[1, 0, 1, 0]`, computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_start_is_one_rule
idris.note: The window of Rete/NetworkClocked.idr, loaded and holding its `Ping` at clock 0, is the one-rule state under the window gate. A TRANSCRIPTION: two definitions coincide, `Refl`; it fails if either is changed and refutes nothing else.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__frame_inv
idris.note: THE FRAME INVARIANT: the view, and the shapes kept against the loaded network. Every working-memory operation and every firing keeps it. The frame's vocabulary, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames.

idris.name: iret_11_3__framed_fires_once_per_match
idris.note: ONCE PER MATCH UNDER THE GENERAL FRAME. From the loaded network, after any inputs applied with no pump between them, a pump that reaches quiescence fires a framed chain exactly as many times as it has matches when the pump begins: its activations are its distinct matches ([IRET.7.7], [IRET.11.1], in the view), each fires once and none twice ([IRET.11.3], [LDET.5.3], in the run), whatever the other rules emit and withdraw meanwhile. Rete/NetworkOnce.idr's theorem with the action-free frame replaced by this one; the plain network, so no cascade and no sweep. Every hypothesis is discharged by computation at `ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_is_an_instance`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__a_is_framed
idris.note: A IS FRAMED: computed over the loaded program.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__b_is_not_framed
idris.note: B IS NOT: A writes kind 1, which B reads. Computed; the frame refuses what it should.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__count
idris.note: HOW OFTEN AN ORDINAL FIRED in a trace. The frame's vocabulary, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__count_hit
idris.note: The count steps on the counted ordinal.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__count_miss
idris.note: And stands on any other.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__count_step
idris.note: One more when the ordinal is the one counted; by pattern matching, so a proof reduces it by rewriting the test alone. The frame's vocabulary, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__emit_one
idris.note: A's RHS: emit a kind-1 fact. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__emit_two_withdraw
idris.note: B's RHS: emit a kind-2 fact and withdraw its own kind-1 fact. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__framed
idris.note: FRAMED: no rule of the program -- the chain's own included -- writes into the chain. A Bool over the loaded alphas and chains, so that a witness checks it by computation; syntactic, since an emit names its schema. The frame's vocabulary, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__framed_rule
idris.note: Under the frame, no kind a rule of the program writes is one the chain reads.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__kind_or
idris.note: A kind, or none, in front of a list. The frame's vocabulary, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__kind_or_elem
idris.note: A kind in front of a list, or not: a member of the list is a member.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__reads
idris.note: THE KINDS A CHAIN READS: the schema of each node's alpha, positive and NOT nodes alike; the dangling node's schema is 0, of which it admits nothing. The frame's vocabulary, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__reads_same
idris.note: Alphas of one shape read alike.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__run_frame
idris.note: THE RUN UNDER THE FRAME, on the traced plain run: over any fuel, from any state with the invariant, a framed chain's tuples never change, its firings in the trace are exactly its activations that went from unfired to fired, and if the run halts `Quiescent` every one of them fired. Whatever the other rules do, however the run halts: fuel is not assumed to suffice.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__step_frame
idris.note: ONE FIRING UNDER THE FRAME: the invariant is kept, and the framed chain is as it was unless it is the rule that fired, when exactly the activation selected, unfired before, is marked and nothing else of the chain moves. The firing rule's RHS, emits and withdraws alike, leaves the framed chain because none of its writes is a kind the chain reads.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_inputs
idris.note: THE INPUTS: two kind-0 facts, with no pump between them. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules
idris.note: THE PROGRAM: three schemas; rule A reads kind 0 and emits kind 1; rule B reads kind 1, emits kind 2 and withdraws its own fact. A is framed, nothing writes kind 0; B is not, A writes what B reads. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_fires_twice
idris.note: And the number is two: A had two matches when the pump began and fired twice. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_is_an_instance
idris.note: THE THEOREM AT THE FIXTURE: every hypothesis discharged by computation -- the frame, the chain as the inputs left it, the run, the halt -- and the count of A's firings is the number of its matches. Executed; what makes the theorem not vacuous.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_trace
idris.note: THE TRACE: A fires for its first match, emitting a kind-1 fact that gives B a match; A fires for its second; then B fires twice, each time emitting and withdrawing its own fact. `[0, 0, 1, 1]`, quiescent. A fired twice for its two matches while B's RHS wrote between. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__writes
idris.note: A chain's rule's writes, against the alphas. The frame's vocabulary, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__writes_emit
idris.note: An emit's kind is among the rule's writes.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__writes_into
idris.note: A RULE WRITES INTO A CHAIN when some kind it writes is one the chain's nodes read. The frame's vocabulary, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__writes_of
idris.note: THE KINDS A RULE WRITES, from its positive kinds and its actions: an emit's kind; a withdraw's, the positive kind at the withdrawn position. The frame's vocabulary, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__writes_withdraw
idris.note: A withdraw's kind, the positive kind at its position, is among the rule's writes.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_7__do_action_frame
idris.note: ONE ACTION of a rule that does not write into the chain leaves the chain and keeps the invariant: an emit asserts its kind, a withdraw retracts a fact of the rule's positive kind at that position, and neither kind is one the chain reads.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_7__do_actions_frame
idris.note: THE RHS of a rule that does not write into the chain leaves the chain, action by action.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__emitted
idris.note: A KIND SOME RULE OF THE PROGRAM EMITS: a chain of the program with an emit of that kind among its actions. The frame's vocabulary with truth maintenance, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames or of rows.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__rows_emitted
idris.note: EVERY ROW TARGETS AN EMITTED KIND: a live fact carrying a row's target id is of a kind some rule of the program emits. With unique ids, that is the fact a cascade retracts for the row. The frame's vocabulary with truth maintenance, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames or of rows.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__rows_live
idris.note: EVERY ROW'S TARGET IS LIVE: what the cascade's fixpoint leaves, and what a mint relies on so that a fresh id is no row's target. The frame's vocabulary with truth maintenance, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames or of rows.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__tms_inv
idris.note: THE FRAME INVARIANT WITH TRUTH MAINTENANCE, within an action: the plain frame invariant, unique fact ids, every row targeting an emitted kind. The frame's vocabulary with truth maintenance, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames or of rows.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__tms_inv_live
idris.note: BETWEEN ACTIONS: the invariant, and every row's target live. The state every operation starts from and the cascade returns to. The frame's vocabulary with truth maintenance, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames or of rows.

idris.name: iret_11_3__framed_fires_once_per_match_ttl
idris.note: ONCE PER MATCH UNDER THE GENERAL FRAME, WITH TRUTH MAINTENANCE AND THE CLOCK. From the loaded clocked network, after any inputs -- data events and ticks that sweep -- prepared with no run between them, a run that reaches quiescence fires a framed chain exactly as many times as it has matches when the run begins, whatever the other rules emit and withdraw and whatever their endings cascade: a cascade's targets are emitted kinds, which a framed chain does not read. Rete/NetworkFrame.idr's theorem on the engine Rete/NetworkClocked.idr runs; a prepare that re-times is outside it and is Rete/NetworkFrameRetime.idr's. Every hypothesis is discharged by computation at `ltim_2_5_1__one_fact_is_an_instance_ttl`.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_net_frame
idris.note: Any number of phases skips a framed chain.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_net_frame
idris.note: THE CASCADE SKIPS A FRAMED CHAIN. A CASCADE'S TARGETS ARE EMITTED KINDS: a row is recorded by a logical emit and targets the fact that emit left live, so what a cascade retracts is of a kind some rule of the program emits, which under the frame no framed chain reads.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_step_net_frame
idris.note: ONE PHASE SKIPS A FRAMED CHAIN: what it retracts are targets of rows, so facts of emitted kinds, which the chain does not read.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_ids_net_frame
idris.note: RETRACTING IDS SKIPS A CHAIN that reads none of their kinds: every fact retracted is looked up by its id and is of a kind the chain does not read, so dispatch leaves the chain.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__a_is_framed_ttl
idris.note: A IS FRAMED in the loaded program, B first or not. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__admits_all
idris.note: THE ALPHA TEST OF THE FIXTURES: admit every fact. Named so that a literal state names it rather than spelling a lambda. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__alphas_three
idris.note: THE ALPHAS: three schemas, kinds 0, 1 and 2, admitting every fact. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__emits_elem
idris.note: An emit's kind is among the rule's emits.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__emits_of
idris.note: THE KINDS A RULE EMITS: an emit's kind; a withdraw emits nothing. What a cascade can target. The frame's vocabulary with truth maintenance, under the clause it serves; the clause says nothing of frames or of rows.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__emits_writes
idris.note: An emitted kind is a written kind: Rete/NetworkFrame.idr's `writes_of` contains `emits_of`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__emitted_not_read
idris.note: UNDER THE FRAME, NO EMITTED KIND IS ONE THE CHAIN READS: an emitted kind is written, and the frame forbids every rule of the program to write a kind the chain reads. The sentence that makes a cascade skip a framed chain.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__entity_chain_ttl
idris.note: THE CHAIN AS THE ENTITY INPUTS LEFT IT: A holds the replacement's match, unfired; the replaced wrapper's ended with it. Read off the literal.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__entity_fires_once_ttl
idris.note: And the number is one: the replacement's match, fired once. Read off the literal.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__entity_inputs_ttl
idris.note: THE ENTITY INPUTS: the entity asserted, replaced with a new payload, re-asserted unchanged; a relation asserted and asserted again. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__entity_is_an_instance_ttl
idris.note: THE THEOREM AT THE ENTITY FIXTURE: A's firings are its matches, 1, the replacement's; the replaced wrapper's is gone and the no-ops made none. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__entity_ready_ttl
idris.note: THE NETWORK AS THE ENTITY INPUTS LEFT IT, as a literal: the replace retracted the first wrapper and minted the new one against the memory the old was still in, id 1, A's activation the new wrapper's and unfired; the two no-ops changed nothing; the relation took the freed id 0. Computed once.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__entity_trace_ttl
idris.note: THE TRACE FROM THE ENTITY STATE: A fires for the replacement's match, B fires and cascades, `[1, 0]`, quiescent; the entity and the input relation, which no row targets, are left live. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__fuel_out_count_ttl
idris.note: THE COUNT EQUATION AT `FuelOut`, read at its instance: A's unfired activations after, 1, plus its firings in the trace, 1, are its unfired activations before, 2; the all-fired conjunct is not claimed. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__life_entity
idris.note: THE LIFECYCLES OF THE ENTITY FIXTURE: kind 0, the kind A reads, an entity; kind 2 a relation; kind 1 explicit. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__no_ttl
idris.note: THE TTL OF THE FIXTURES: none, for every kind. Named so that every statement of the two-fact run spells it the same way and the checker compares statements syntactically rather than by evaluating the run. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_fact_fires_once_ttl
idris.note: And the number is one: A had one match when the run began and fired once, through B's cascade. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_fact_is_an_instance_ttl
idris.note: THE THEOREM AT THE FIXTURE: the frame and the chain as the input left it discharged by computation, the run and the halt by the trace, and the count of A's firings is the number of its matches, through B's cascade. Executed; what makes the theorem not vacuous.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_fact_ready
idris.note: THE NETWORK AS THE INPUT LEFT IT: the loaded clocked network at clock 0, the input prepared, no run after it. A holds one match, unfired; B holds none. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_fact_ready_chain
idris.note: THE CHAIN AS THE INPUT LEFT IT: A, at ordinal 1, holds the one match, unfired, after the prepare's sweep, assert and cascade. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_fact_trace_ttl
idris.note: THE TRACE, AND THE CASCADE: A fires for its match and emits a kind-1 fact; B, now matched and at the lower ordinal, fires next, emitting its kind-2 fact and withdrawing the kind-1 fact it matched, which ends its activation, and the cascade that follows retracts the kind-2 fact it had just recorded. `[1, 0]`, quiescent, and only the kind-0 fact remains: no kind-2 fact survives its justifier. Executed, with fuel 3.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_input_ttl
idris.note: THE INPUT OF THE ONE-FACT FIXTURE: one kind-0 fact, whose run evaluates as one `Refl`. The two-fact run, with B's cascade between A's two firings, does not evaluate as one `Refl` within the lane's wall clock (dev-mcp jobs ds-00275 and ds-00277, past 1,800 s where the proofs alone take 644 s); it is `ltim_2_5_1__two_facts_run_ttl`, firing by firing from literal states, as Lcyc/TmsWitnesses.idr has. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rows_emitted_append
idris.note: A FRESH FACT IS NO ROW'S TARGET: with every row's target live, a fact whose id is not live, appended to any part of the memory, keeps the row property. Where fact-id reuse is ruled out: a stale row could name a reused id, and the cascade's fixpoint leaves no stale row.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rows_emitted_record
idris.note: A RECORDED ROW targets a live fact of an emitted kind; with unique ids that fact is the only one carrying the id.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rows_emitted_sub
idris.note: Fewer facts and fewer rows keep the row property.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rules_b_first
idris.note: THE RULES, Rete/NetworkFrame.idr's two with B loaded first: B reads kind 1, emits kind 2 and withdraws its own kind-1 fact; A reads kind 0 and emits kind 1. B at the lower ordinal is selected as soon as A's firing gives it a match, so B's firing and the cascade its withdrawal starts fall inside A's run. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__run_frame_ttl
idris.note: THE RUN UNDER THE FRAME on the clocked network: over any fuel, from any state between actions with the invariant, a framed chain's tuples never change, its firings in the trace are exactly its activations that went from unfired to fired, and if the run halts `Quiescent` every one of them fired. Whatever the other rules do and whatever their endings cascade, however the run halts: fuel is not assumed to suffice.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__step_frame_ttl
idris.note: ONE FIRING UNDER THE FRAME on the clocked network: the invariant is kept, and the framed chain is as it was unless it is the rule that fired, when exactly the activation selected, unfired before, is marked. The cascade of every action is inside: it retracts targets of rows, of emitted kinds, which the chain does not read.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ticked_chain_ttl
idris.note: THE CHAIN AS THE TICKED INPUTS LEFT IT: A holds the one match the sweep left, unfired. Read off the literal.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ticked_fires_once_ttl
idris.note: And the number is one: of A's two matches before the second tick the sweep ended one, and A fired once for the other. Read off the literal.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ticked_inputs_ttl
idris.note: THE TICKED INPUTS: a kind-0 fact at clock 0 (deadline 2), a tick to 1 that expires nothing, a second kind-0 fact at clock 1 (deadline 3), a tick to 2 that expires the first. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ticked_is_an_instance_ttl
idris.note: THE THEOREM AT THE TICKED FIXTURE: A's firings are its matches after the sweep, 1; the expired fact's match is not among them. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ticked_ready_ttl
idris.note: THE NETWORK AS THE TICKED INPUTS LEFT IT, as a literal: the first fact swept at the second tick, its deadline at the clock, gone from working memory, its alpha memory and A's activations; the second live with its deadline ahead; the swept fact's row kept in the deadline table until its id is minted again; the clock at 2. Computed once.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ticked_trace_ttl
idris.note: THE TRACE FROM THE TICKED STATE: A fires for the surviving match, B fires and cascades, `[1, 0]`, quiescent, the kind-0 fact alone left live. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ttl_two
idris.note: THE TTL OF THE TICKED FIXTURE: two for kind 0, none for the rest. Named so that every statement spells it the same way. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_facts_fires_twice_ttl
idris.note: And the number is two: A had two matches when the run began and fired twice, with B's firing and cascade between them. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_facts_fuel_out_ttl
idris.note: THE RUN THAT RUNS OUT OF FUEL: the two-fact fixture with fuel 1 -- A fires for its first match and the fuel is spent, `FuelOut`, trace `[1]`, B's match made and unfired, A's second match unfired. One firing as a `Refl` from the literal, then the run with no fuel, chained.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_facts_is_an_instance_ttl
idris.note: THE THEOREM AT THE TWO-FACT FIXTURE: the frame and the chain as the inputs left it by computation, the run and the halt by the chain of firings, and the count of A's firings is the number of its matches, through B's two cascades, one of them between A's firings. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_facts_ready_chain
idris.note: THE CHAIN AS THE TWO INPUTS LEFT IT: A, at ordinal 1, holds its two matches, unfired, in assertion order. Read off the literal.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_facts_ready_ttl
idris.note: THE NETWORK AS THE TWO INPUTS LEFT IT, as a literal: the loaded clocked network at clock 0, both inputs prepared, no run after them; A holds two matches, unfired, in assertion order, B none, no rows, no deadlines. Computed once; the other claims reach the prepared network through this equation.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_facts_run_ttl
idris.note: THE TWO-FACT RUN, FIRING BY FIRING: A fires for its first match; B, matched and at the lower ordinal, fires next, records the row for its kind-2 fact, withdraws the kind-1 fact it matched and the cascade retracts the kind-2 fact; A fires for its second match, minting the withdrawn id again; B fires and cascades again. `[1, 0, 1, 0]`, quiescent, only the two kind-0 facts left. Each firing a `Refl` from a literal state, chained by `iret_11_4__run_ttl_net_traced_cons` as Lcyc/TmsWitnesses.idr does; the four-firing run as one `Refl` is beyond the type-level evaluator within the lane's wall clock. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_inputs_ttl
idris.note: THE TWO INPUTS: two kind-0 facts, prepared with no run between them. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_entity
idris.note: THE ENTITY PROGRAM: the two rules, B first, with kind 0 an entity. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_tms
idris.note: THE PROGRAM: kind 2 is a relation, so B's emit records a row and B's withdrawal ends the activation that recorded it; kinds 0 and 1 are explicit. A fixture.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_7__do_action_tms_frame
idris.note: ONE ACTION WITH TRUTH MAINTENANCE under the frame, from a state between actions: the core action leaves the framed chain and keeps the frame invariant (Rete/NetworkFrame.idr), unique ids and the row property; the record targets an emitted kind of the firing rule; the cascade leaves the framed chain and ends between actions again.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_7__do_actions_ttl_frame
idris.note: THE RHS on the clocked network leaves a framed chain and keeps the invariant, action by action; the deadline table rides beside.

idris.name: iret_11_3__framed_fires_once_per_match_clocked
idris.note: Once per match through the tick that re-evaluates the condition: a match the tick makes true fires once, a match it makes false does not fire, under the frame.

idris.name: iret_19_5__tick_inv
idris.note: The frame invariant under the clause, kept through the tick that decides the clause's edges.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__a_is_framed_gated
idris.note: The framed chain of the opening fixture, its re-timed node read for its alpha alone. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__a_is_framed_shutting
idris.note: The framed chain of the shutting fixture. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__b_shutters
idris.note: Which rule carries the condition that closes: B's. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__emit_two
idris.note: A logical emit with no withdraw, so the match that recorded the row outlives the firing. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ended_fired_cascade
idris.note: What ending a fired match does to what it recorded: its row goes and its logical fact is retracted. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ended_fired_chain
idris.note: A condition that closes ends the match, executed on a FIRED match: no activation remains. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__fact_then_tick
idris.note: A fact, then the tick that re-evaluates the condition over it. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__fired_ready
idris.note: The network with the fact asserted while B's condition is open. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__fired_row
idris.note: B's row, recorded by its firing under the open condition. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__fired_run
idris.note: The run in which B fires under the open condition and records its row. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__fired_then_tick
idris.note: The tick on which B's condition closes, after its match fired. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__fired_trace
idris.note: A and B fire once each; B's match is live and fired after the run. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__gate_open_match
idris.note: Before the condition closes it is true and the match is live, unfired. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__gate_shut_no_match
idris.note: Before the edge the condition is false and there is no match. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__gated_clock
idris.note: The clock the edge is read at, 1, after the tick. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__gated_fires_once
idris.note: One edge, one firing. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__gated_is_an_instance
idris.note: The theorem at the opening fixture: one firing for the one match the edge made. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__gated_ready
idris.note: The network after the edge: the condition true, the match live and unfired. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__gated_ready_chain
idris.note: The false-to-true edge, executed: the tick re-evaluates the condition true and the match is a new, unfired activation.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__gated_trace
idris.note: The match the edge made fires once, with B's cascade inside the run. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__gates
idris.note: Which rule carries the time-dependent condition the tick re-evaluates: A's. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__opens_at_one
idris.note: A time-dependent condition that becomes true at clock 1: the false-to-true edge of the clause. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rules_b_shutting
idris.note: The two rules with the condition that closes on B, the rule that records a row. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rules_gated
idris.note: The two rules with A's condition the opening gate. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rules_shutting
idris.note: The two rules with A's condition the shutting gate. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__shut_fires_none
idris.note: A condition closed, nothing fired. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__shut_is_an_instance
idris.note: The theorem at the shutting fixture: no firing for no match. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__shut_ready
idris.note: The network after the condition closed: the match ended. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__shut_ready_chain
idris.note: A condition that closes ends the match, executed: the tick re-evaluates it false and no activation remains, fired or not.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__shut_trace
idris.note: The ended match does not fire. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__shuts_at_one
idris.note: A time-dependent condition that becomes false at clock 1: the condition that closes. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__shutters
idris.note: Which rule carries the condition that closes: A's. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__swept_chain
idris.note: The framed chain after the swept tick: no match. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__swept_fires_none
idris.note: Swept, then no edge, no firing. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__swept_is_an_instance
idris.note: The theorem at the swept fixture: no firing for no match, the fact gone before the edge. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__swept_ready
idris.note: The network after a tick that swept the fact and re-evaluated the condition: no match. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__swept_ready_ttl
idris.note: The sweep before the re-evaluation, executed: the condition opens on nothing. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__swept_trace
idris.note: Nothing to fire after the swept tick. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ttl_one
idris.note: A TTL that expires the fact at the tick the condition would open on. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_b_shutting
idris.note: The program with B's emit logical under the closing condition. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_gated
idris.note: The program with the opening gate. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_shutting
idris.note: The program with the shutting gate. A fixture.

idris.name: iret_11_3__refraction_after_history
idris.note: 'Resets each pump' is consistent with the model in the tick-free fragment: a reset at the pump's input is one of [IRET.11.3.2]'s clearings, and clearings refuse nothing. The per-fact one-shot the clause needs for time-gated rules is item 4's, with [LDET.5.8].

idris.name: iret_11_3__framed_fires_once_per_match_sampled
idris.note: Once per match through samples taken at every input: a match a sample makes true fires once, under the frame.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__arrives_open
idris.note: A fact arriving at the sample the condition becomes true at. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__arrives_open_chain
idris.note: The false-to-true edge at a data input's sample, executed: the match is a new, unfired activation. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__arrives_open_fires_once
idris.note: One edge, one firing. Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__arrives_open_is_an_instance
idris.note: The theorem at the fixture: one firing for the one match. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__arrives_open_ready
idris.note: The network after that arrival: the condition true, the match live and unfired. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__arrives_open_trace
idris.note: The match the edge made fires once, with B's cascade inside the run. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__fact_then_tick_is_steps
idris.note: The opening fixture of Rete/NetworkFrameRetime.idr reached as two sampled steps. Computed.

idris.name: lthe_2_5_1__is_framed
idris.note: A sequence chain under the general frame. Computed.

idris.name: lthe_2_5_1__pairs_is_an_instance
idris.note: Once per match, for a sequence's matches. Executed.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__rising
idris.note: A gate that stays true once true: `now() > t`, the shape of every example in the clauses.

idris.name: ldet_5_8__late_fires_once
idris.note: THE CLAUSE'S OBSERVABLE, on the network: assert one Ping, pump twice with the gate shut, advance the clock past it, pump twice more -- `late` fires exactly once, in the third pump.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_2__unfired_are_born
idris.note: After a quiescent pump a tick leaves unfired only the matches it made: what the next run fires is exactly what the tick made true.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__closing_ends
idris.note: A CONDITION THAT CLOSES ENDS THE MATCH: after a tick, under the view, no activation is left whose match the new test refuses, fired or not. The match ends and its activation with it, as a `within` window's does; no memory of the firing outlives the activation.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__edge_once
idris.note: EDGE-ONCE for a gate that stays true once true: two ticks, the second starting no earlier than the first ends, never both make the same match, so with `ltim_2_4_2__unfired_are_born` a match fires in at most one pump, on the tick its condition goes false to true. 'Must not re-fire on subsequent ticks while the condition remains true', on the engine with time-dependent tests and no tables. A gate that closes and reopens is a new edge, as the clause requires: `ltim_2_5_1__closing_ends`, `ltim_2_5_1__reopening_is_unfired`, and the executed `ltim_2_5_1__second_edge_refires`. On the engine with the tables, Rete/NetworkTwoClocks.idr's `ltim_2_5_1__rising_fires_at_most_once` is the count over any history.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__reopening_is_unfired
idris.note: A REOPENING IS A NEW EDGE: an activation of a match the tick made is unfired, whatever was fired before the gate shut. Under the view no old activation can carry that match, since the old test refused it; so it is one the tick made, and the tick makes its activations unfired.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__second_edge_refires
idris.note: THE SECOND EDGE FIRES AGAIN, as the clause requires: one `Ping`, one wrapper, never retracted; the window `(now() > 0 and now() < 2) or now() > 2` opens at 1, shuts at 2, reopens at 3. The rule fires in the first pump and in the third, `[1, 0, 1, 0]`: once per opening. Computed; what the clause says.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window
idris.note: `(now() > 0 and now() < 2) or now() > 2`: open at 1, shut at 2, open again from 3 -- the clause's window that shuts and reopens. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_gate
idris.note: The window as a time-dependent join test. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_loaded
idris.note: The rule under the window loaded at clock 0: one alpha for Ping, one positive node carrying the window, an RHS that only logs. A fixture.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_3__on_delay_fires_once
idris.note: 'Fire once per false to true edge ... and must not re-fire on subsequent ticks while the condition remains true': a `dwell` gate stays true once true, and the pump at 6 fires nothing. Executed.

idris.name: lcdb_3_2_3__retracted_before_t_fires_nothing
idris.note: No edge for a wrapper that left working memory before the condition held. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__dwell_window
idris.note: A `dwell` WINDOW that shuts and reopens: `(dwell >= 2 and dwell < 4) or dwell >= 6`, logical/LTIM.2.5.1_window_reopens's gate. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__dwell_window_reopens
idris.note: A `dwell` WINDOW THAT SHUTS AND REOPENS FIRES ONCE PER OPENING: ticks 1 to 6 each followed by a pump; the window opens at 2, shuts at 4, reopens at 6 -- logical/LTIM.2.5.1_window_reopens's shape. 'A window that shuts and reopens fires once per opening.' Executed: `[[], [(0, True)], [], [], [], [(0, True)]]`.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__within_fires_once
idris.note: Once per opening for a `within` window, which opens at entry and shuts once. Executed.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__at_most_once_timed
idris.note: A rising gate's edges over any history sum to at most one: once per edge, and one edge.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__fires_on_the_first_due_tick_timed
idris.note: Once per rising edge, and the edge is at the first sample that reaches `fire_at`.

idris.name: ltac_5_1__timer_counts_are_edges_timed
idris.note: The firings over a history are the gate's rising edges, one count per pump: once per false-to-true edge.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__edge_at_ext
idris.note: An edge is decided by the gate's two readings, so two gates that read alike at every clock make one edge. By congruence.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__edge_of
idris.note: AN EDGE from two readings of a gate: 1 when it was shut and is open, 0 otherwise -- Rete/NetworkEdges.idr's `edge_at` at the two readings, named so that an equality of readings lifts to an equality of edges by congruence. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__edges_ext
idris.note: Over a history: the edges of two gates that read alike at every clock are one list. By induction; what lets Rete/NetworkAfter.idr's results, stated on the `fire_at` gate, be read on the `dwell` gate.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__rising_b
idris.note: 'A gate that stays true once true', as a predicate of the clock.

idris.name: lexp_9_5_1__dwell_fires_once_executed
idris.note: 'A gate that stays true once true fires once per wrapper', executed under `dwell >= 2`: `[0, 1, 0, 0]`, total 1.

idris.name: lexp_9_5_1__dwell_gate_rising
idris.note: WHICH GATES CAN REOPEN: `dwell >= d` is rising, so 'a gate that stays true once true fires once per wrapper' is what it does; only a gate that reads the wall clock can reopen.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__edge_at_true
idris.note: A tick from an open gate is no edge.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rising_edges_at_most_one
idris.note: C3a. A RISING GATE'S EDGES OVER ANY TICK HISTORY SUM TO AT MOST ONE: it rises once or not at all, because the composed engine's clock never goes back. 'A gate that stays true once true fires once per wrapper', as a count.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rising_edges_none
idris.note: Once a rising gate has opened, no later tick is an edge.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rising_fires_at_most_once
idris.note: C3a ON THE ENGINE, with part B: the one-fact program under a rising gate fires AT MOST ONCE over any tick history from any starting clock. Once per false-to-true edge, and a rising gate has at most one. The hypothesis is inhabited by `lexp_9_5_1__dwell_gate_rising` and executed by `lexp_9_5_1__dwell_fires_once_executed`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__total
idris.note: The number of false-to-true edges over a history.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_gate_reopens
idris.note: 'A `now()` gate the wall clock crosses back and forth fires once per opening': `[1, 0, 1, 0]`, computed.

idris.name: ldet_5_8__late_fires_once_timed
idris.note: 'Fire once per false to true edge ... and must not re-fire on subsequent ticks while the condition remains true', for a `now()` gate. Executed.

idris.name: llog_3_11_1__clock_where_retracts_timed
idris.note: 'A condition that closes ends its match': the match ends at the pump at 3, with no change to its fact. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__alphas_two
idris.note: Two alphas, the Sensor's kind 0 and an unrelated Other's kind 1. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__expired_fact_cannot_reopen_timed
idris.note: AN EXPIRED FACT CANNOT REOPEN: the same window and advances with the Ping under a TTL of 2; open at 1 and fired; the tick to 2 sweeps the Ping, whose deadline is at the clock, before the pump; the window opens at 3 on nothing -- logical/LTIM.2.5.1_expired_fact_cannot_reopen's shape. 'Once per false-to-true edge of a live match', and the fact is not live. Executed: `[[(0, True)], [], [], []]`, and working memory empty.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__explicit_life
idris.note: An explicit lifecycle for every kind: the expired-fact fixture's Ping has no key. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__now_edge_once_multipump_timed
idris.note: EDGE-ONCE OVER FURTHER TICKS: after the gate opens at 6 and fires, the advances to 7 and 8 with the gate still true fire nothing -- logical/LTIM.2.5_now_edge_once_multipump's shape. 'Must not re-fire on subsequent ticks while the condition remains true.' Executed: `[[], [(0, True)], [], []]`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__now_window
idris.note: THE WINDOW on the wall clock: `(now() > 0 and now() < 2) or now() > 2`, the witnesses' window of [LTIM.2.5.1] in their units. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ttl_two
idris.note: A default TTL of 2 on every kind. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__unrelated_change_timed

Executed: `[[], [(0, True)], [], []]`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_second_edge_refires_timed
idris.note: A WINDOW THAT SHUTS AND REOPENS FIRES ONCE PER OPENING: the Ping asserted at (0, 0); advances to 1, 2, 3 and 4, each followed by a pump; open at 1, shut at 2 (the match ends), open again at 3 (a new match), still open at 4 -- logical/LTIM.2.5.1_window_second_edge_refires's shape. Executed: `[[(0, True)], [], [(0, True)], []]`.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_2__now_edge_once_rearm_timed
idris.note: Once per edge of a live match: the first wrapper's one edge, then the second's. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__at_one
idris.note: A gate that can shut and reopen as the wall clock moves. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_gate_reopens_timed
idris.note: 'A condition that closes ends its match, and reopening it is a new edge': once per opening, under a wall that goes 1, 2, 1, 2. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__lapse_row_dead
idris.note: A condition that closes ends the match, executed on the fixture's row: no fired activation of it after the tick to 1.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__lapse_state
idris.note: Rete/NetworkFrameRetime.idr's shutting-gate fixture, at the point between the sweep and the re-time. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__lapse_wm
idris.note: The fixture's working memory before the gate shuts, as a literal. Computed.

tla.name: ltim_2_5_1__newpump
tla.note: A pump boundary. Under this clause edge-once is a consequence of refraction with [LDET.5.8], and a pump boundary clears no identity ([IRET.11.3]). The model keeps the event because the refused reading `pump`, which resets refraction each pump, is decided on it.

tla.name: ltim_2_5_1__pumpNo
tla.note: The pump number. Under this clause it scopes no refraction; it is the scope of the refused reading `pump`, and it stamps each firing in the observable.
